mechanism: Impulse cluster indicators CCp / Complex_pairs: each currency has a line in an 8-currency cluster; pair balance is the intersection of the two pair currencies (or Complex_pairs signal line vs zero). That cross marks a direction-change candidate for the pair, but must be filtered by higher-TF / trend-following cluster state so counter-trend impulse crosses are ignored.
data_needed: Cluster of up to 8 FX majors; CCp or Complex_pairs (or Complex_pairs1) buffers; optional higher-TF trend filter from CCFp/CFP.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD examples; USDJPY H4 impulse walkthrough; cluster of eight currencies; params tuned for TF ≥ H4
why_new_for_mis: Cross-pair currency-relative impulse sensor: regime change is detected from multi-currency cluster balance, not from the single pair’s own oscillators—so MIS can flag pair turns that incorporate all cluster members’ co-movement.
quote: When the lines intersect, the balance of the pair currencies is achieved. As a rule, the achievement of the balance point shows that the direction will probably change, i.e. a signal appears.

mechanism: Trend-following cluster indicators CCFp (pair lines visible) and CFP (pair vs balance): inertial because they fold in higher timeframes. Green/red periods mark when bull vs bear impulse signals are preferred; they do not fire entries themselves but gate the impulse cluster.
data_needed: CCFp and/or CFP on the analyzed pair inside the same multi-currency cluster; higher-TF-aware parameters.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD with CCFp/CFP; cluster of eight currencies; inertial vs H4+
why_new_for_mis: Separates cluster-derived trend preference (regime) from impulse crosses (change), giving MIS a two-layer FX-cluster state: which side of the pair is structurally preferred before acting on fast balance flips.
quote: As distinct from signal indicators, trend-following indicators do not give trade signals, but they show the general trend, i.e. point out, which signals are more preferable at this moment of time - bull or bear.

mechanism: Sum of all currency lines in CCFp/CCp is zero each bar. A currency above zero is overbought, below zero oversold; near zero is equilibrium. For a pair, CFP/Complex_pairs signal vs zero maps tension. Projecting successive balance intersections onto price (Complex_balance) yields a horizontal line in flat and a sloping line in trend; slope changes mark fade vs renewal of the move.
data_needed: Full cluster currency lines; pair CFP/Complex_pairs; optional Complex_balance projection onto the price chart.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD with marked A–F balance segments; eight-currency cluster
why_new_for_mis: Turns the cluster zero-line into an explicit FX overbought/oversold + flat-vs-trend geometry on price—MIS can tag pair tension and whether the equilibrium level itself is trending.
quote: The horizontal balance line on the price charts shows that the currency pair is in flat. If it is sloping, the pair is in trend.

mechanism: On Complex_pairs: identify a sharp fractal peak after a strong move, draw a signal line through a subsidiary supporting peak; aggressive entry when the indicator crosses that line, confirmed when it later crosses the zero/balance line. Grade strength: A (subsidiary in oversold/overbought) strong; B (subsidiary near zero) weaker; C (balance crossed before signal line) weakest; post-cross divergence is rare and strongest.
data_needed: Complex_pairs (original preferred on small TFs vs Complex_pairs1); fractal and subsidiary-peak geometry on the indicator pane.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USDJPY H4 examples Buy_N/Sell_N; Complex_pairs1 also usable on stocks/futures/commodities
why_new_for_mis: Structured impulse-signal taxonomy on a cluster-derived oscillator (fractal→subsidiary→cross→balance confirm with A/B/C grades)—a graded change sensor, not a raw zero-cross.
quote: For determining a signal we need a clearly expressed Fractal - a sharp peak, which, as a rule, appears after strong movements. The second element is the presence of a subsidiary (supporting) peak.

mechanism: Observe 4–6 minute charts of symbols well correlated with the traded symbol; combinations of their concurrent movement dynamics are treated as predisposing the next move of the target symbol—a cross-sectional short-horizon lead sensor before acting on the target alone.
data_needed: Synchronized M1 (or tick) paths on a basket of correlated FX symbols plus the target.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Forex multi-symbol; minute charts; author also stresses tick history when available
why_new_for_mis: Frames multi-asset minute co-dynamics as an explicit leading sensor for the target path—MIS can treat correlated-basket micro-structure as a regime/lead feature, not just pair-local TA.
quote: Open several (4-6) minute charts on different symbols well correlated with the symbol you are going to work with. … combination of dynamics movement of some symbols predetermines the movement of other symbols

mechanism: Build a self-organizing trend model on short prehistory, synthesize features of trend dynamics, retrain on every new datum, and emit a two-step forecast (six points ahead, then six more on the prior forecast) finishing before the next M1 bar; optional five-step extension to ~30 points. Emphasizes tick-synced multi-symbol history and feature covariation / GA-like feature grouping over static indicators.
data_needed: Preferably synchronized multi-symbol tick history (years); falling back to short prehistory for self-organizing training; M1 bar clock for online cycle.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any symbol/TF claimed; author’s implementation on minute ticks with <1 minute compute budget
why_new_for_mis: Online self-organizing sequence/trend sensor with chained multi-step forecasts and continuous retraining—closer to a neural/sequence MIS sensor than frozen indicator stacks.
quote: The built model should continue training at each receipt of new data and dynamically trace and forecast not only all market changes, but also detect newly beginning trends of this changes.

mechanism: For each symbol compute daily close minus SMA(CorPeriod) residual; Pearson-style Cor = Σ(u1·u2)/√(Σu1²·Σu2²) over CorPeriod. Block new hedge opens when Cor is outside [And, Between] (defaults 0.9–1.05); open only while correlation stays in-band, with MoveSameWay dictating long/short vs same-side legs (swap-biased).
data_needed: iClose and iMA(SMA, PRICE_CLOSE) on PERIOD_D1 for base and hedge symbols over CorPeriod; MarketInfo spreads/swaps for sizing.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Primary EURJPY & GBPJPY; also cites GBPUSD–EURUSD (same-way) and EURUSD–USDCHF (opposite); CorPeriod default 5 on D1
why_new_for_mis: Turns rolling residual correlation into an explicit coupling-regime gate for multi-symbol exposure—MIS can sense when a pair basket is co-moving enough (or too unstable) to treat as a hedgeable unit.
quote: if(Cor(BaseSymbol, H_Symbol) > Between || Cor(BaseSymbol, H_Symbol) < And) // Block opening when the correlation is out of expected range.
